title: The horosphere through the source, with the target's DIRECTION as the boundary base point
equation: omega = z_target / ||z_target||  (the target's direction, a point of the boundary sphere); b_omega(x) = log( (1 - ||x||^2) / ||x - omega||^2 ); L = -log softmax_j( -| b_omega(x_j) - b_omega(x_source) | / T )  at j = argmin_k ||z_target - c_k||

symbols.z_target / z_source: the host encoder's latent for the target / the source of a train transition
symbols.omega: the target's DIRECTION on the boundary sphere: the base point of the Busemann function
symbols.b_omega: the Busemann function of omega, in the unit ball (curvature -1 after the measured scaling)
symbols.x_j: the j-th level-0 codeword's ball point
symbols.x_source: the source's ball point; its level defines the horosphere the target's code must join
symbols.T: the temperature, locked at specification time at 0.25
symbols.j: the level-0 code the HOST's own Euclidean assignment gives the target, detached

basepoints: a BOUNDARY point: the target latent's direction. This is the correction R10 needs -- a Busemann function is only defined for a point at infinity, and with an interior base point its 'level sets' are geodesic spheres, i.e. r8_09's radial family

domains.manifold: the unit ball (curvature -1 after the measured tangent scaling); the base point omega lies ON the boundary
domains.points: codewords and latents mapped by exp_0 with the measured scale, so c||x||^2 < 1 by construction
domains.boundary: a point with ||x||^2 >= 1 - 0.05 is skipped and counted (F3); the Busemann function is finite everywhere else
domains.distance: no distance is used: the term is the level difference of two Busemann values

why_hyperbolic: The Busemann function of a boundary point does not exist in a Euclidean space: there the horosphere through a point degenerates to a half-space and the level becomes a linear functional. Its curl-free structure, its tangency to the boundary and the fact that the level is signed are properties of negative curvature. A Euclidean twin (the squared distance to omega) loses the tangency: it is a half-space coordinate, so the term would select codewords by a projection instead of by a level set.
role_assignment: One role, the level set: the source fixes the horosphere, the target's codeword must join it. Nothing else is reweighted, and the base point is DERIVED from the target, so there is no free per-item parameter to collapse.

gradient_paths.L: b_omega(x_j) depends on the codewords only; omega and x_source are detached, and the label is the host's detached assignment, so the gradient reaches the codebook and nothing else
gradient_paths.encoder: zero: the base point and the source's level are detached, so the term cannot move the encoder

sid_effect.L1: the level-0 assignment changes; that is the export's only change
sid_effect.L2_L3: unchanged (the host's Euclidean residual chain on zhat)

compatibility.dimensions: 32 (the latent is mapped with the measured tangent scale)

hypotheses: the horospheric level of the source is a quantity a Euclidean term cannot express: it is the level of a Busemann function of a BOUNDARY point, whose level sets are closed and tangent to the boundary, so two codewords at the same distance from the source can be on different level sets

the level is NOT a function of the geodesic distance to any interior point (the verifier measures a rank correlation of about -0.81 against the distance, where a radial quantity would be -1), so constraining it is not r8_09's radial family

because the term moves the codebook and leaves the encoder exactly alone (measured: the encoder's gradient norm is 0.0 and the codebook's is 1.86e-02), the behaviour signal cannot coarsen the content partition
expected_failure_modes: the level's spread is small relative to the codeword level's spread, so the CE cannot separate the codewords: the mechanism must record the gap distribution, not assume it

the loss is a softmax over the level GAPS, so a uniform shift of the source's level cancels: the source enters only through the ORDERING of the code levels around it, and a source perturbation that does not change that ordering leaves the loss unchanged (measured: 0.0 on the probe batch)
the level's sign is one-sided on this data, so the term must not be described as asking which side of the horosphere a codeword is on; that claim is withdrawn

H4_gradient_path.verdict: the term reaches the codebook and leaves the encoder exactly alone

H5_numerical.verdict: the level takes ONE sign on this batch, so the inside/outside question the horosphere carries does not discriminate here; the term degenerates to 'the codeword closest in level to the source'

H6_causal_pathway.note: the loss is a softmax over the level GAPS, so a uniform shift of the source's level cancels: the source only matters through the ORDERING of the code levels around it. A small perturbation that does not change that ordering leaves the loss unchanged, which is what a zero sensitivity means.
H6_causal_pathway.verdict: the source moves the loss only when it changes the ordering

prior_art.r10_hyp_busemann_horosphere: the SAME idea with an INTERIOR base point, which the auditor proved is a near-radial equidistance constraint (level never negative, 25-47% spread on a horosphere). This proposal differs in the one place that matters: the base point is on the boundary
prior_art.r8_07_hyperbolic_gyro_translation: translates points; this takes a level of a Busemann function
prior_art.r8_08_hyperbolic_frechet: a barycentre of successors; this has no barycentre
prior_art.r8_09_hyperbolic_radial_hierarchy: a radial (distance-from-a-centre) hierarchy; a horosphere is NOT a distance sphere, and the measured spearman with the distance to an interior point is -0.77 against r8_09-style -0.9996
prior_art.r8_10_hyperbolic_gw: optimal transport between graphs; this solves no transport
prior_art.literature: the verified literature matrix found NO recommender use of Busemann functions or horospheres (a recorded negative search result), and no Riemannian-VQ paper; Gu et al.'s product spaces and SAHL's Euclidean PCA-block subspaces do not contain this operator

differentiation: Not R10 (boundary base point, signed level, genuine horospheres -- all three measurable), not r8_09 (a horosphere is tangent to the boundary; a distance sphere is not), not a Euclidean half-space term (the tangency is the mechanism).
falsifier: Refuted if (a) the level's rank correlation with the distance to an interior point falls to -0.999 on a real batch (the operator has collapsed back to a radial constraint), or (b) the level gaps cannot separate the host's label from the other codewords by more than the numerical noise, or (c) the encoder's gradient is not exactly zero, or (d) the mechanism's term leaves the L1 export unchanged.

predicted_consequences.ER: no rise predicted; the term routes a behaviour signal into the codebook's level structure, and the failure analysis says ER gains do not transfer
predicted_consequences.G_H1: prediction: unchanged at matched L0 occupancy; a rise with a falling distinct-code count is the Case C artefact
predicted_consequences.Recall_NDCG: prediction: the informative outcome is an L0 partition whose tail is at the control's while the transition pairs align in level; a Case A repeat (a bigger largest cell) refutes it

tests.statement: on points constructed at a constant Busemann level, and on a horosphere built as a Euclidean sphere tangent to the boundary, the level is constant within 1e-9
the term's gradient at the encoder parameters is exactly zero and at the codebook is finite and nonzero
a codeword with ||x||^2 >= 1 - margin is skipped and counted; the remaining codewords' levels are bit-identical to the unguarded path
the pooled codebook gradient equals the independent mean of the four ranks' local gradients within 1e-5
3 tokens per item, every token in [0,255], the L0 histogram uses more than one code

on a real batch the rank correlation of the level with the geodesic distance to an interior point is below -0.95 in absolute value but above -0.999: a value of -1 would mean the operator had collapsed back to a radial constraint

the verifier's Busemann function is constant to 1e-9 on a horosphere built as a Euclidean sphere tangent to the boundary, and the Euclidean twin's level set crosses the boundary instead of touching it
the measurement that motivated this revision: the source's level takes one sign on the frozen batch, so the declaration must not claim a signed level
the distribution of the level gaps separates the host's own label from the other codewords by more than the numerical noise; a mechanism that cannot separate them is inert

a codeword whose level leaves the declared band is skipped and counted; the remaining codewords' levels are bit-identical to the unguarded path

mechanism.summary: the target's codeword joins the horosphere through the source

cgv_gaps: G1-G6 can only run once the mechanism is implemented; no executable claim is made here

G3 is declared as invariants (finite, nonzero) because oracles.py has no formula oracle for a Busemann level; the mechanism-specific checks b1_level_is_signed and b1_not_a_radial_function are the substitute, and they are tests, not gates

revision.trigger: the JOIN E measurement: on the frozen batch the source's Busemann level takes ONE sign, and the base-point study shows five candidate base points all do the same, so the inside/outside question cannot be made discriminative on this data
revision.dropped_claim: that the level is SIGNED and therefore asks which side of the horosphere a codeword is on -- the data never puts the source on both sides, so that claim was inert
revision.kept_claim: the target's codeword must sit at the same horospheric LEVEL as the source, where the level is a Busemann function of a boundary base point: its level sets are closed and tangent to the boundary, and it is NOT a function of the geodesic distance to any interior point
